conceptTag: A safe bet or a risky one?
readerTitle: The big order: four calls that decide if it's safe
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (골판지 상자 공장 + 밀키트 앱 고객) · 모든 수치와 인물은 설명용
insight: 좋은 베팅은 맞히는 것이 아니라 네 가지를 차례로 묻는 것이다. 보통 어떻게 되는가, 평균적으로 얼마인가, 최악에도 살아남는가, 새 정보로 얼마나 고칠 것인가.
misconception: 기대값이 플러스면 안전한 베팅이다. 또는 위험해 보이면 피하는 것이 안전하다.

sources.text: 확률적 사고의 표준 개념 (기저율, 기대값, 파산 위험, 믿음 갱신, 평균 회귀)

factChecks.note: 과거 고객 기록(10곳 중 3곳 약속대로 성장, 4곳 더 느리게, 3곳 축소·폐업)은 이야기 속 가상 데이터입니다. 실제 스타트업 생존율 통계로 읽히지 않도록 카드에 'your own records'로 적었습니다.
현금 결제 시 잔액: $500,000 − $400,000 = $100,000. 리스 비용은 구체적 수치를 쓰지 않고 '평균적으로 더 비싸다'로만 표현했습니다.

cards.title: The big order: four calls that decide if it's safe
body: Mara runs a box factory with 40 staff. A fast-growing meal-kit app wants boxes, and lots of them: three times what her biggest customer buys.
It could make her year. It could also sink the factory. You'll make four calls in her place.

image.label: A small box factory with a huge stack of orders arriving
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 아담한 골판지 상자 공장 앞에 휴대폰 화면에서 쏟아져 나온 듯한 거대한 주문서 더미. 공장 주인이 클립보드를 들고 올려다봄. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: The founder says they'll grow 4x next year.
body: Mara checks her own records. Of the 10 fast-growing startups she has supplied, 3 grew as promised, 4 grew more slowly, and 3 shrank or closed.

options.text: Plan on 4x growth. The founder knows the business best
options.feedback: She'd build for the best case, which happened only 3 times in 10. Founders' forecasts tend to be hopeful.

options.text: Start from her records, then adjust for what's special about this customer
options.feedback: She gets a realistic starting point and still uses what she knows about this app. The founder's pitch becomes one clue, not the plan.

options.text: Turn it down. Startups are too unreliable
options.feedback: She avoids the 3-in-10 downside, but also gives up the 7 in 10 that grew at least somewhat.

cards.title: The order needs a $400,000 machine.
body: Say you started from the records. Mara estimates the extra profit over three years:

image.label: Three branches showing three possible outcomes
image.brief: 가지가 셋으로 갈라지는 나무 다이어그램. 각 가지에 '3 in 10 · $1,000,000', '4 in 10 · $500,000', '3 in 10 · $100,000'. 가지 굵기를 확률에 비례하게. 밑동에 '$400,000 machine'.

options.text: Buy it. The best case pays back 2.5 times
options.feedback: The answer may be right, but the reasoning only looks at one branch. The same logic would approve bets that lose money on average.

options.text: Skip it. There's a 3-in-10 chance of losing $300,000
options.feedback: She'd avoid that loss but walk away from a bet that pays well on average.

options.text: Weigh all three: on average it returns about $530,000, above the $400,000 cost
options.feedback: Each outcome counts in proportion to its chance. On average the bet earns about $130,000 more than it costs.

cards.title: How should Mara pay for it?
body: Say you went ahead. The factory has $500,000 in cash. A good average is no use if one bad branch ends the business.

options.text: Pay cash. It's the cheapest option overall
options.feedback: Cheapest if things go well. But it leaves $100,000 of cushion, and in the 3-in-10 case the customer is gone and the machine sits idle.

options.text: Lease it with a buyout option, and ask the app for a one-year minimum order
options.feedback: It costs more on average, but the worst case becomes survivable. She pays a little to stay in the game.

options.text: Borrow against the factory building to keep cash
options.feedback: Cash stays safe, but the worst branch now puts the building itself at risk.

cards.softwareNote: A software company faces the same call when one big client asks for custom features. If losing that client would leave a team and a product built for nobody, get a commitment first.

cards.title: Month one: a record.
body: Say you leased. In the first month, orders come in 50% above plan, the factory's best month ever. The app asks Mara to reserve a second machine now.

options.text: Lease a second machine right away
options.feedback: One record month is often part luck, and the next tends to land closer to normal. She could end up with two machines for one machine's work.

options.text: Raise her estimate a little, and decide after three months of data
options.feedback: She treats the news as real but not final. Waiting costs a little speed and buys a clearer picture.

options.text: Ignore it and stick to the original plan
options.feedback: It guards against a lucky spike, but refusing to update means real growth would catch her short.

cards.title: The spike settled. The trend held.
body: Months two and three came in about 15% above plan: less than the record, but still ahead.
Mara nudged her odds. "Grows as promised" now looked closer to 4 in 10. In month five she leased a second machine on the same terms, with the same minimum order.

image.label: Monthly orders: one tall spike, then steady bars above the plan line
image.brief: 월별 주문량 막대 그래프. 첫 달만 크게 튀고, 이후 막대들은 점선 'Plan' 위에 약간 높게 안정됨. 첫 달 막대에 'Record month' 라벨.

cards.title: The numbers are guesses, and one bet is one bet.
body: Mara's odds came from 10 past customers. That's a small sample, so treat it as a rough guide, not a fact.
An average only shows up across many bets. On a single bet she'll get one branch, not $530,000. A sound decision can still lose money, so judge it by the reasoning, not only the result.

cards.title: A safe bet is one you've checked four ways.
body: Each of Mara's calls used one idea from this unit:
list: **Decision 1 · Base rates:** start from what usually happens
**Decision 2 · Expected value:** weigh every outcome by its chance
**Decision 3 · Risk of ruin:** make sure the worst case is survivable
**Decision 4 · Updating beliefs:** move your estimate a little with each new fact, and expect record months to settle
cards.callout: **Try it today:** take one bet on your desk. Write three outcomes, a rough chance for each, and what the worst one would do to you.
